newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to close four embassies, open one new one.
newsitem.headline: France to close four embassies, open one new one.

text.p: France will close four embassies, three of them in Africa, while opening one new embassy in Turkmenistan, in response to changing priorities and budgetary needs, Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Friday.

The disclosure that Paris planned a new embassy in Ashkhabad in Turkmenistan was made three days ahead of Turkmenistan President Saparmurat Niyazov's arrival in Paris for a three-day visit beginning on Monday.
France plans to shut down embassies in Kingston, Jamaica; Freetown, Sierra Leone; Monrovia, Liberia, and Lilongwe, Malawi, the minister told a meeting of French citizens living abroad.
Jamaican affairs will be turned over to France's embassy in Trinidad and Tobago, while Sierra Leone and Liberia will be handled by Paris's embassy in Ghana, he said.
Matters of interest to France in Malawi will be taken care of by the French embassy in Lusaka, Zambia, de Charette said.
The government has been under pressure to slash public spending in order to help France qualify for a single European currency from 1999.
